Busk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Busk, Ukraine

Demolished. This is one of the oldest Jewish cemeteries in Ukraine, home to mainland Ukraine's oldest surviving Jewish tombstone, dated 1520, alongside around ten more from the 16th century. Busk's Jewish community dates to 1454 and survived the devastating Khmelnytsky massacre of 1648, later becoming home to both Belz and Olesko Hasidic followers. By 1900 about 2,340 Jews lived here; many later emigrated to the US. Nazi occupation from July 1941 culminated in a Yom Kippur massacre on September 21, 1942, when around 700 Jews were shot, followed by a ghetto and labor camp liquidated in 1943. A 2004 monument marks the mass-shooting site within the cemetery itself.
